response.sql: WITH joined AS (SELECT tr.ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS count FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg GROUP BY tr.ordertypedist), totals AS (SELECT SUM(count) AS total_count, COUNT(*) AS distinct_mixes FROM joined), shares AS (SELECT j.ordertypedist, j.count, CAST(j.count AS NUMERIC) / CAST(t.total_count AS NUMERIC) AS share, 1.0 / CAST(t.distinct_mixes AS NUMERIC) AS avg_share FROM joined j CROSS JOIN totals t) SELECT ordertypedist AS mix, count, share, share - avg_share AS above_avg FROM shares WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC;

assumptions.assumption: When multiple advanced behaviour analyses reference the same transaction, that transaction is counted multiple times in the share calculation—once per analysis. This interprets 'taking the advanced behaviour analyses' as iterating over analyses rather than unique transactions.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each distinct transaction only once, regardless of how many advanced behaviour analyses reference it. This would treat the set of linked transactions (not analyses) as the population for share calculation.
alternatives.sql: WITH joined AS (SELECT DISTINCT tr.transreg, tr.ordertypedist FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg), counts AS (SELECT ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS count FROM joined GROUP BY ordertypedist), totals AS (SELECT SUM(count) AS total_count, COUNT(*) AS distinct_mixes FROM counts), shares AS (SELECT c.ordertypedist, c.count, CAST(c.count AS NUMERIC) / CAST(t.total_count AS NUMERIC) AS share, 1.0 / CAST(t.distinct_mixes AS NUMERIC) AS avg_share FROM counts c CROSS JOIN totals t) SELECT ordertypedist AS mix, count, share, share - avg_share AS above_avg FROM shares WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC;
